Subject: Dedicated capacity question: H100/A100/L4 trade-offs for our workload

Hi Grace,

We chatted briefly at the conference — thanks again. We're building an internal inference platform (RAG + chat) and evaluating partner options for dedicated capacity. High-level:
- Expected steady-state: ~120 QPS (avg), spiky peaks to ~400 QPS for 30-45 minutes/day.
- Model mix: majority 13B decoder-only models (generation), occasional 70B encoder-decoder variants for higher-fidelity RAG contexts, and a small set of lightweight 7B/LLM variants used for embeddings and assistant fallbacks.
- Latency target: 95p < 300ms for single-turn chat; embeddings can be looser.
- Security: need private deployment (VPC) and SOC2 evidence.

Questions: is there a clear recommendation on SKU mix (H100 vs A100 vs L4) given throughput + memory needs? We're particularly unsure whether L4 is a viable lower-cost option for generation at our latency SLO, or only for embeddings and caching. Also: any rough monthly cost delta vs throughput targets you can point to?

If helpful, I can share a short query profile and 7-day peak trace. Looking to scope a pilot in Oct.

Thanks — Alex

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question: H100/A100/L4 trade-offs for our workload

Alex — great to meet you too. Quick read of your high-levels below; happy to take a deeper look once you share the 7-day trace. For now, a pragmatic starter recommendation based on similar customers:

High-level, two-pronged approach (pilot -> scale):
1) Pilot (4–6 weeks): mixed A100 + L4 for cost control; include 1–2 H100 instances to validate 70B RAG memory needs. A100s are a good middle ground for 13B generation with good throughput per-dollar; H100s give headroom for large KV/cache-resident 70B contexts. L4s are excellent for embeddings and high-concurrency, low-memory fallbacks — not usually primary inference for 70B models under tight latency SLOs.

2) Scale (post-pilot telemetry): promote H100s into steady reserved capacity if 70B traffic exceeds ~10–15% of tokens or memory pressure is frequent. Otherwise scale A100 fleet and keep L4 for edge/highly concurrent routes.

Initial configuration we often propose:
- Reserve: 6 x A100 (for 13B, batching, and most generation traffic)
- Reserve: 1 x H100 (for warm 70B RAG contexts)
- On-demand/burst: pool of 4–8 L4s (for embeddings, fallbacks, and bursty embedding/low-latency requests)

Risks & notes:
- If your 70B models require long context KV caches, H100 is effectively mandatory for predictable latency.
- Quantization (4-bit) can make A100s serve larger models with throughput gains, but quality/regression testing is required.
- Batching helps unit cost but can hurt 95p latency; Redwood Optimize recommendations can tune batching windows per route.

I've attached a quick calculator (fleet-fit-calc.xlsx) with conservative throughput assumptions so you can plug in your traces. Ben (cc) will help turn this into a pilot quote.

Would you be available for a 30-min pilot-scope call on Wednesday?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity question: H100/A100/L4 trade-offs for our workload

Adding a technical breakdown — copied from internal notes for quick paste to the customer.

Assumptions from Alex: 120 avg QPS, 400 spike QPS, model mix ~ majority 13B, ~10% 70B peak.

Memory & model fit:
- 13B decoder-only (FP16): ~25–30GB RAM footprint; fits comfortably on A100-40GB or A100-80GB with room for batching and KV cache.
- 70B (FP16) with 32k context and KV cache: 60–90GB depending on implementation; H100-80GB or H100-96GB variants give deterministic headroom.
- L4 is 24–32GB class (varies by vendor) — good for 7B/13B pruned/quantized variants but will struggle for full 70B.

Throughput (rough, highly workload dependent):
- A100 (13B, optimized kernels, quantized): ~400–800 tokens/sec per GPU with moderate batching.
- H100 (70B, kernels tuned): ~250–600 tokens/sec per GPU for large-context RAG workloads (larger KV overhead reduces effective throughput).
- L4 (13B quantized lightweight): ~800–1500 tokens/sec but only for shorter contexts and trimmed models.

Operational controls to hit 95p < 300ms:
- Separate routes by SLO and route to appropriate pool (H100 for large-context strict latency; A100 for best price/latency balance; L4 for cheap embedding/low-cost fallbacks).
- Use KV caching aggressively for RAG (prefix caches + persistent KV store) to reduce token compute on hot contexts.
- Configure adaptive batching: short windows for SLO routes (1–5ms), longer windows for throughput-oriented routes.

Cost/hedging guidance:
- Start with minimal H100 (1–2) to avoid over-committing; measure p95/p99 under production traffic.
- Commit to A100 reserves if steady-state utilization > 60% across the pilot month.
- Keep L4s as burst/on-demand to flatten peak cost without changing baseline.

Potential risks we should call out to the customer:
- Model growth: customers often move to larger context sizes; plan for +20–30% memory growth over 12 months.
- Quantization regressions: 4-bit can reduce memory but requires eval set to validate.
- Scheduling complexity: mixing SKUs increases placement complexity; we recommend Redwood Console SLO routing and automated fallbacks.

I've summarized these points in the attached appendix. We should include a short margin buffer in the pilot quote for unexpected token volume.

-Markus
Principal Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sku-risk-appendix.pdf (pdf)]
